Common Signs of Addiction Families Miss

The early signs of addiction are usually subtle, which is exactly why families miss them for months or years. 

Behavioural signs include withdrawing from friends and family, missing work or important commitments, secrecy around whereabouts or spending, and mood swings that seem disproportionate to the situation. 

Physical signs can include changes in sleep patterns, sudden weight change, bloodshot eyes, or a decline in personal grooming. Psychologically, someone struggling with addiction often shows increasing irritability when the substance isn't available, repeated promises to cut back that don't hold, and a growing tolerance — needing more of the substance to get the same effect. In India specifically, cultural pressure to maintain appearances often means families notice these signs but avoid naming them directly, which can delay treatment by years. None of these signs alone confirms addiction, but a consistent pattern across several of them is worth taking seriously. At 

Veda, our clinical team offers confidential assessment calls to help families understand whether what they're observing warrants professional evaluation, without any pressure to commit to treatment on that first call. Reach out to us.

What Alcohol Detox at a Rehab Centre Actually Involves

Alcohol detox is the medical process of managing withdrawal once someone stops drinking, and it's the part of treatment people tend to fear most — often unnecessarily, when it's done properly. 

At a rehab centre, detox typically begins with a medical assessment covering physical health, drinking history, and any other conditions, since withdrawal severity varies significantly between individuals. 

For moderate to heavy drinkers, withdrawal symptoms can include tremors, anxiety, sweating, insomnia, and in more severe cases, seizures or delirium tremens — which is precisely why unsupervised home detox can be genuinely dangerous. In a supervised setting, medication is used where needed to manage symptoms safely, vital signs are monitored, and a doctor is available around the clock during the highest-risk window, usually the first three to five days. 

At Veda, detox is followed immediately by structured therapeutic care rather than a gap before treatment starts — our clinical team stays involved from the first day through discharge planning. Detox alone doesn't resolve addiction; it's the physical starting point that makes the psychological work possible. Get in touch to understand what detox would look like for your specific situation.

Getting Treatment for a Family Member Who Drinks

Getting alcohol addiction treatment for a family member is rarely as simple as booking an appointment — it usually starts with a conversation that hasn't happened yet, or has happened badly. 

A few things tend to help: speaking to a treatment professional yourself first, before approaching the person, so you understand what to expect and how to frame the conversation without triggering defensiveness. 

Choosing a calm, private moment rather than confronting someone mid-crisis or after drinking. Being specific about behaviour you've observed rather than general accusations, and being clear about what you're asking for — an assessment call, not necessarily an immediate commitment to residential treatment. If the person is resistant, a structured family intervention, guided by a professional, is sometimes necessary. 

At Veda, our clinical team offers confidential pre-admission calls specifically for family members in this position — we can help you think through timing, wording, and what to do if the first attempt doesn't work. Our centres in Mumbai, New Delhi, Bengaluru, and Gangtok also support family therapy once someone is admitted. You don't have to plan this alone. Get in touch whenever you're ready to talk.

How to Evaluate a De-Addiction Centre in India

India has a wide range of de-addiction centres, from free government facilities to boutique private ones, and the right choice depends heavily on the specific situation. 

Government-run de-addiction centres are accessible and important, particularly for emergency detox, but typically operate at high volume with limited one-on-one clinical time. Private de-addiction centres, like 

Veda's four locations in Mumbai, New Delhi, Bengaluru, and Gangtok, take a different approach — capping capacity at 5 to 8 clients per centre and maintaining a near 1:1 therapist-to-client ratio, so treatment can be closely tailored rather than delivered on a fixed group timetable. A good de-addiction centre, regardless of budget, should offer medically supervised detox, evidence-based therapy named specifically rather than vaguely, and some capacity to address co-occurring mental health conditions, since addiction and mental health issues frequently overlap. Aftercare planning matters just as much as the initial stay — what happens in the weeks and months after discharge often determines long-term outcomes more than the programme itself. If you're trying to evaluate options for yourself or someone you love, get in touch for a direct, no-obligation conversation.

What to Look for in an Alcohol Rehab Centre

Is detox medically supervised on-site, with a doctor available around the clock during the highest-risk withdrawal period? 

Is psychiatric care integrated into daily treatment, or only available through occasional outside referral? 

What is the therapist-to-client ratio — a centre managing 30 clients per therapist cannot offer the same attention as one managing closer to one-to-one? 

Does the programme name its therapeutic approach specifically — CBT, DBT, EMDR, Motivational Interviewing — or describe it only in general terms like "counselling sessions"?
